analysis.title: Stay invested as volatility tests market fundamentals (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: The S&P 500 rose 2.5% last week, its first weekly gain in five weeks and the largest since August, as investors weighed fundamentals against developments in technology, inflation and geopolitics.

UBS expects this week's calendar (NVIDIA Q3 earnings, a new AI developer listing on the Nasdaq, multiple Fed speakers, the APEC Summit in Shenzhen) to keep volatility elevated, but says fundamentals remain constructive enough to stay invested.

UBS retains conviction in the structural AI opportunity without taking single-name views. It forecasts aggregate AI capital spending of USD 1tr this year and USD 1.4tr in 2027, and expects cloud revenue growth to accelerate further.
UBS argues that uncertainty over chip restrictions and financing and execution risks call for selectivity and diversification within AI.
October US consumer prices rose more than expected, while core producer prices rose 0.3% m/m, slowing from an upwardly revised 0.8% in September.

The latest inflation data raises the risk that the Fed shifts from gradual quarterly hikes to consecutive 25bp hikes. UBS expects this week's Fed speakers to be more balanced than recent hawkish remarks from Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan and Governor Christopher Waller.
UBS says current elevated yields offer meaningful return potential for high-quality fixed income.

UBS sees significant geopolitical breakthroughs as unlikely in the near term and advises against major portfolio changes on geopolitics alone. It suggests broad commodities, hedge funds and select real assets to limit sensitivity to shocks.
Japan's Q3 GDP contracted at an annualized 0.1%, the first decline in four quarters and worse than the +0.3% consensus. Private consumption fell 0.3% against an expected 0.2% decline.

UBS views Japan's weak GDP as less concerning given its composition (fading temporary Q2 support, delayed oil shipments). It expects improvement and expects the Bank of Japan to raise rates in December 2026 and March 2027.
earnings_insights: NVIDIA is scheduled to report third-quarter results on 17 November (not yet reported). UBS says investors will look for evidence that overall AI demand remains strong and can generate sufficient returns to justify higher infrastructure spending.
